question: In A.R. Wilfley & Sons v. National Union, how did the Colorado Supreme Court say the umbrella/excess policy should be read in deciding whether the primary insurer's insolvency triggered it?
reference_notes: Must mention: the policy is read as a whole, harmonizing its provisions so none is meaningless; the parties intended first-dollar obligations only when an occurrence falls outside the coverage of a scheduled underlying policy; nothing indicated insolvency turns a covered occurrence into an uncovered one.
cited_authority: Pub. Serv. Co. of Colo. v. Wallis &Cos., 986 P.2d 924, 933
rater_a_reason: cl11452592:14 states the whole-policy and harmonizing approach, the intended trigger for first-dollar obligations and that insolvency does not turn a covered occurrence into an uncovered one.

question: According to the Colorado Supreme Court in Wilfley, how did the Tenth Circuit in Scott's Liquid Gold interpret an umbrella policy's reference to occurrences 'not covered' by underlying insurance?
reference_notes: Must mention: the Tenth Circuit read 'not covered' as an event that does not meet the definition of a covered event in the underlying policies, i.e., risks not insured; it refused a strained reading that would make the umbrella insurer reimburse defense costs after exhaustion because the parties could have said so expressly.
cited_authority: Unigard Mut. Ins. Co. v. Mission Ins. Co., 907 P.2d 94, 99
rater_a_reason: cl11452592:16 describes the Tenth Circuit's reading of 'not covered' as risks not insured, and its refusal of a strained interpretation absent express language.

question: Under Robbins v. Mason County Title Insurance, when does a Washington insurer's duty to defend arise and when is the insurer relieved of it?
reference_notes: Must mention: the duty to defend is broader than the duty to indemnify and arises if the policy conceivably covers the insured; the insurer is relieved only if the policy clearly does not cover the claim; an ambiguous complaint is liberally construed in favor of triggering the duty.
cited_authority: Truck Ins. Exch. v. VanPort Homes, Inc., 147 Wn.2d 751, 760
rater_a_reason: cl4532507:6 states the broader-than-indemnity rule, the conceivable-coverage trigger, relief only if clearly not covered, and liberal construction of ambiguity.

question: Why did the Illinois Supreme Court in Sheckler v. Auto-Owners hold that its earlier decision in Dix did not decide whether the insurer owed the tenants a defense?
reference_notes: Must mention: Dix was a subrogation case governed by equitable principles, whereas the claim here was a third-party contribution claim and the issue was the duty to defend or indemnify; Dix expressly limited its holding to the particular facts of that case; the court therefore looked to the policy language.
rater_a_reason: cl9226166:11 states that Dix is a subrogation case governed by equity, that the issue here is not subrogation, and that Dix was limited to its particular facts.

question: How did the Washington Supreme Court in Robbins classify the Tribe's treaty right to harvest shellfish from the insured's tidelands, and what reasoning supported that classification?
reference_notes: Must mention: the right is a profit (the right to sever and remove a substance from the land) rather than an easement (a right to enter and use property); the court analogized it to timber-cutting rights treated as a profit a prendre.
cited_authority: Affil. FM Ins. Co. v. LTK Consulting Servs., Inc., 170 Wn.2d 442, 458
rater_a_reason: cl4532507:11 defines easement and profit, compares the Tribe's right to timber-cutting rights, and holds the right is a profit.

label: supported
cited_authority: State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Co. v. Elmore, 2020 IL 125441, ¶ 19
rater_a_reason: Step 1: cl9226166:8 quotes Valley Forge for comparing the underlying complaint's facts to the policy and Zurich for the indemnity trigger.
construction_note: Paraphrase of the two quoted rules in paragraph 31 of chunk 8.

claim: Umbrella coverage extends the scope of coverage horizontally and provides first-dollar coverage where the underlying primary insurance affords none, while excess coverage extends vertically and attaches only after the underlying limits are exhausted.
label: supported
cited_authority: Apodaca v. Allstate Ins. Co., 255 P.3d 1099, 1103
rater_a_reason: Step 1: cl11452592:10 (paragraphs 36-37) says umbrella coverage runs horizontally and provides first-dollar coverage where primary insurance affords none, and excess coverage extends vertically and attaches only after exhaustion.
construction_note: Paraphrase of paragraphs 36 and 37 of chunk 10.

claim: The Washington Supreme Court held that a tribe's letter asserting a right to harvest shellfish was a 'demand' under the title policy, so the duty to defend was triggered even though no legal proceedings had begun, because the policy covered both demands and legal proceedings.
label: right_doc_wrong_passage
cited_authority: Truck Ins. Exch. v. VanPort Homes, Inc., 147 Wn.2d 751, 760
rater_a_reason: Step 2: the cited cl4532507:6 states the general duty-to-defend rules; the 'demand' holding based on policy language is in cl4532507:9.
construction_note: Claim paraphrases cl4532507:9 (same opinion); cited chunk cl4532507:6 is the preceding general statement of the duty to defend and does not address demands or the policy wording.

claim: An insurer acts in bad faith if its breach of the duty to defend was unreasonable, frivolous or unfounded, and an insurer unsure of its duty may defend under a reservation of rights while seeking a declaratory judgment.
label: wrong_document

construction_note: Claim paraphrases the first two sentences of cl4532507:15; cited chunk is from the Colorado Wilfley opinion.

claim: The Illinois Supreme Court held that Dix was inapplicable because Dix limited coinsured status to tenants whose leases expressly obligated the landlord to purchase fire insurance.
label: unsupported_claim
cited_authority: Valley Forge Insurance Co., 223 Ill. 2d at 362
